I will keep this year practical and familiar. I have farmed for a long time, and with only 9 mu and some family labor working off-farm, I will not spread myself too thin or take risks on complicated changes. I will keep my main wheat-maize rotation on most of the land because that is the backbone of my farm and gives me stable grain. I will keep some land in cotton because I know how to manage it and it brings cash, but I will not put too much land into it because it takes more labor. I will also keep a smaller mungbean area because it is useful as a lower-input crop and fits well when I want to reduce cost and labor pressure. Since I have well irrigation, I will use water at the key stages rather than irrigating too often. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it matters for stable emergence and yield, and I will keep fertilizer moderate and crop-specific. For wheat and maize, I will feed them more because they are my main output crops. For cotton, I will use moderate fertilizer and watch pests closely. For mungbean, I will keep inputs lighter because I do not want to overspend on a crop that is mainly there for flexibility and some income.
